detect-names-and-quotes-no-score:
Yes, heavily. Line by line:

- **"In today's fast-paced digital landscape"** — banned opener (E5) plus AI vocabulary (*landscape*, B1). Says nothing.
- **"isn't just a tool - it's a partner"** — the negative-parallelism contrast (B3): setting up a negation just to knock it down, and doing it in the first sentence.
- **Em dash** used as a stylistic hinge (C1) — a strong tell on its own.
- **"stands as a testament to"** — copula avoidance (B2) plus significance inflation (A1). "Is" would do the job.
- **"pivotal"** — reflexive AI vocabulary (B1), doing no real descriptive work.
- **"seamless, vibrant collaboration"** — brochure adjectives (A4), stacked for effect rather than meaning.
- **"empowering teams to unlock their full potential"** — vague declarative (A7): asserts significance without saying what actually happens. What does the platform *do*? The sentence never says.

Underneath all that: there's no actual content. Strip the tells and nothing is left — no feature, no claim, no specific. That's the bigger giveaway than any individual phrase: it's not describing a product, it's performing enthusiasm about one.

Dear Orla,

My name is Dan, and I run ScentVerdict, a fragrance review site I started last year after getting frustrated with how hard it was to find honest reviews of niche perfumes.

We test every fragrance thoroughly. Each review is based on at least two weeks of wear, and we score longevity, projection and value separately, because a single star rating hides too much. Over the last twelve months we have published 2,400 reviews, and our readers tell us the separate scores are the reason they come back.

I have been following your house for a while, and I think your approach to small-batch releases is exactly the kind of story our readers care about. I would love to review your autumn collection, and I would be happy to share our methodology in more detail, including how we handle samples, how we disclose free products, and how we make sure the review is independent of any commercial relationship.

We also run a monthly newsletter that goes to our most engaged readers, and we have a small but growing presence on Instagram and TikTok, where short wear-test videos have done particularly well.

Please do reach out if this sounds interesting. I would be delighted to set up a call at a time that suits you.

Kind regards,
Dan
